[[File:Knudemutation.svg|thumb|350px|The [[prime knot|prime]] '''Kinoshita–Terasaka knot''' (11n42<!--Dowker-Thistlethwaite-->) (left) and the prime [[Conway knot]] (11n34<!--Dowker-Thistlethwaite-->) (right) showing how they are related by [[mutation (knot theory)|mutation]]]]

In [[knot theory]], the '''Kinoshita–Terasaka knot''' is a particular [[prime knot]] with 11 crossings.<ref>{{cite web |title=Conway's Knot |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ConwaysKnot.html |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en |access-date=2020-05-19}}</ref> It is named after Japanese mathematicians Shinichi Kinoshita and Hidetaka Terasaka, who wrote about it in 1957.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Kinoshita, S. |author2=Terasaka, H.  |title = On Unions of Knots|journal = Osaka Math J.|volume = 9|year = 1957|pages = 131-153}}</ref> The Kinoshita–Terasaka knot has a variety of interesting mathematical properties.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Tillmann |first=Stephan |date=June 2000 |title=On the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot and generalised Conway mutation |journal=Journal of Knot Theory and Its Ramifications |language=en |volume=09 |issue=4 |pages=557–575 |doi=10.1142/S0218216500000311 |issn=0218-2165 |url=https://www.maths.usyd.edu.au/u/tillmann/papers/kino.pdf}}</ref> It is related by [[mutation (knot theory)|mutation]] to the [[Conway knot]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Mutant Knots |last=Chmutov |first=S.V. |date=2007 |website=people.math.osu.edu |url=https://people.math.osu.edu/chmutov.1/talks/2007/OSU-10-25-2007/mutants.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612193043/https://people.math.osu.edu/chmutov.1/talks/2007/OSU-10-25-2007/mutants.pdf |archive-date=2020-06-12}}</ref> with which it shares a [[Jones polynomial]]. It has the same [[Alexander polynomial]] as the [[unknot]].<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t9XICgAAQBAJ&q=KINOSHITA-TERASAKA+KNOT&pg=PA151 |title=Geometries of Nature, Living Systems and Human Cognition: New Interactions of Mathematics with Natural Sciences and Humanities |isbn=9789814479455 |last1=Boi |first1=Luciano |date=2 November 2005}}</ref>
